newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet says co-founder sold shares.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet says co-founder sold shares.

text.p: One of ValuJet Inc's four co-founders sold a big chunk of stock in the company over a four business-day period beginning a day after the discount carrier got final U.S. government approval to resume scheduled flights, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
ValuJet spokesman Gregg Kenyon said Timothy Flynn, a non-executive board member, sold 955,000 shares between Sept. 27 and Oct. 3, while his family sold 90,000.
On Sept. 26, the U.S. Department of Transportation ended a three-month grounding of the airline by declaring ValuJet fit to fly again.
"I can only assume he was trying to diversify his holdings," Kenyon said when asked to comment on the sale.
ValuJet stock rose 25 percent to 12-7/8 on the day approval was granted. But it has since fallen. On Wednesday, the share price was off 1/4 at 10-1/4.

Flynn also sold 1.5 million shares in the aftermath of the May 11 Florida Everglades crash of ValuJet Flight 592, which killed 110 people and precipitated a period of intense federal safety inspections that led to the airline's grounding in mid-June.
Following the latest sale, Flynn holds about 3.5 million ValuJet shares or about 58 percent of the six million he held before the Everglades crash.
